evaluation: Out-of-time and blocked cross-validation of the full predict() pipeline (cleaning, features, ridge models, rule layer) on the 27 healthy weekdays, scoring every 15-min interval including the zero-energy nights: models refit on data before 2021-11-01 / 11-08 / 11-15 and scored on all later healthy days gave RMSE 0.77 / 0.64 / 0.74 kWh, and leave-one-block-out over 6 day-blocks gave about 0.73; typical-profile-by-time-of-day alone is about 0.95, the same interval on the previous day is 1.1 and 1-hour persistence is 2.3 kWh, so I quote 0.8 kWh to leave room for regime shift in the unseen period. Causality was verified by truncating the file at T-45min and by corrupting every row at or after T-45min (garbage, -999, text, reordering, duplicates) at 23 cut-offs: the forecast for T never changed.
data_findings: Target: chilled_water_energy is per-5-min kWh; the forecast target is the sum of the 3 readings in each 15-min interval. The AHU runs on a fixed weekday schedule (fan on 08:00-08:05 to 18:40) and the meter reads exactly 0 outside it, so the target is bimodal: 0 at night, about 6.7 kWh per 15 min in steady state, about 7-8 in the 08:00-08:45 start-up, a pull-down bump at 18:15 (about 9.4, varies 5-15 by day) and about 4.3 at 18:30. Day-to-day level varies with std about 0.9 kWh per interval and is the main thing the lagged anomalies track. A model must therefore know the schedule (time of day) and the day level; I use a typical time-of-day profile plus ridge regressions on the anomaly vs that profile seen up to T-50min, per segment (start-up / steady / shut-down).

Row order and duplicates: 10,800 rows but only 10,512 unique timestamps. 288 rows (2021-11-15 01:10 to 11-16 01:05) are an exact replay of earlier rows, and the block 2021-10-28 21:00-23:25 is written in reverse order (timestamps are right, values are smooth only after sorting). predict() sorts by time and keeps the first record of a repeated timestamp.

Gaps: only weekdays are present (no Saturdays/Sundays), plus a 12 h hole on 09-23/24 and two multi-week holes (2021-10-02 to 10-24 and 2021-11-18 to 12-08). Nothing is interpolated across gaps; windows are NaN-aware and the forecast falls back to the time-of-day profile when no recent data exists. Forecasts are issued for every 15-min slot (also inside gaps and up to 72 h past the last record).

Sentinels and text: 17 readings of chilled_water_energy equal -999 (also in the middle of working hours) and 14 outdoor_relative_humidity values are the string 'OFFLINE'. Both become NaN; any 15-min interval with a missing reading is excluded from training targets.

Unit change: indoor air_temperature switches to Fahrenheit (about 80-85) from 2021-11-08 (mixed during that day); rows above 45 are converted to Celsius. dry_bulb_temp has a 50.7 C outlier, removed by a plausibility range. Other columns have spikes (voc 3922 ppb, illuminance) that are not used.

Chilled-water meter faults (the important one): (1) from 2021-09-20 18:40 to 2021-10-26 10:30 (about 35 days) the meter reads 0 while the AHU runs at full fan speed with the cooling valve open, and supply_air_flow is stuck at 93.15 CMH, then NaN, then 0, i.e. an offline meter, not zero cooling; (2) 2021-11-03 19:00 to 11-04 10:30 the meter is frozen at 0.48 kWh per reading; (3) on 2021-11-17 after about 14:30 it becomes erratic (0, 0.15, 13.6 spike) and then reads 0 with the AHU running; (4) catch-up spikes of 14.4 kWh (09-13 17:25, after 9 zero readings = 9 x 1.6) and 13.6 kWh (11-17) are accumulations after drop-outs, so readings above 8 kWh are treated as invalid. I excluded these stretches from training and profile estimation (they would teach the model that a running AHU uses no energy). In predict() they are detected causally (reading 0 while fan > 20 Hz and valve command > 20 %, or at least 6 identical positive readings), removed from the lag features, and if a fault has lasted 1 h the forecast persists the fault (0 or 3 x frozen value) until a healthy reading appears, because if the same fault recurs the truth will probably show it.

Abnormal days: 2021-11-04 (public holiday) the AHU starts at 10:05 instead of 08:05 and occupant_count is 0; supply_air_flow has 1,816 NaNs and damper_position 2,436 NaNs (sensors unavailable); occupant_count is 0 all day on several days (sensor offline). These are not used as features. Rules: AHU seen off for >= 15 min after 09:00 -> forecast 0 (late start / holiday); weekend with AHU off -> 0; AHU working outside 08:00-18:40 -> persist the recent level.

Time stamps carry a constant +08:00 offset (Singapore, no DST); the offset is dropped and the forecasts are indexed by naive local interval start. Level drift: the first September days are much lower (about 4.6-5 vs 6-8 kWh steady state), so the model works with anomalies relative to a typical profile and updates with the last hour, today's mean and the previous days' mean.
